clue.text: Atmosphere changed in empty Berkshire cinema

indicators.note: the letters are changed round into a new order
an empty word keeps only its shell, so only the outside letters of Berkshire are used

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cinema in Berkshire has had a makeover and now feels different.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves BE from Berkshire; 'changed' rearranges BE plus CINEMA.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the mood or feeling of a place is its atmosphere.

clue.text: Chapter at start of book penned by key US author

indicators.note: something penned by another is enclosed by it, as if in a pen

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
OT, the Old Testament, is the opening part of the Book, the Bible

explanation.surface: A chapter at the opening of a book, written by a key American writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Book' is the Bible in crosswords, which starts with OT, the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisa May Alcott was the American novelist who wrote Little Women.

clue.text: Originally bran flakes a caterer distributed?

definitions.text: Originally bran flakes a caterer distributed?

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter of the word bran
the letters of flakes a caterer are distributed, spread around in a new order

explanation.surface: A caterer serving up bran flakes at the start of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: B (first of 'bran') plus an anagram of FLAKES A CATERER signalled by 'distributed'; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bran flakes are a classic morning grain dish handed out by a caterer.

clue.text: Interpret old proposal one introduced

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: one introduced means the numeral is put inside the plan

parts.note: a plan is a proposal
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asked to make sense of a former proposal that brought in one change.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to interpret something is to make its meaning clear.

clue.text: Pressure to stuff Indian pancake

indicators.note: to stuff is to fill, so the pressure letter goes inside the Indian

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: An instruction for filling an Indian pancake, perhaps a dosa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' looks like cuisine from India but is a member of the Cree nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin French griddle cake is a crêpe.

clue.text: Confused group of workers wanting right offer

parts.note: TU is a trade union, an organised group of workers
a bid is an offer at auction

explanation.surface: A muddled trade union that wants its offer to be the correct one.
explanation.definitionFit: Turbid can mean muddled in thought as well as cloudy water.

clue.text: Dig up from plateau near Thiepval

indicators.note: from signals that the letters are taken out of the run of words plateau near Thiepval

explanation.surface: Excavating relics from the Somme battlefield near the village of Thiepval.
explanation.walkthrough: Thiepval is a French village on the Somme, site of a First World War memorial.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dig up is to excavate from the ground.

clue.text: Features of licensed bowling alley: great fun

definitions.meaning: a pub-style alley serves ale and has pins to knock down
the phrase 'life isn't all ...' means pure pleasure

explanation.walkthrough: Skittles is a pub game like tenpin bowling, played in British pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for pure enjoyment is the same as the literal pub pairing of ale and a pin game.

clue.text: Some Europeans munched nuts, having tons to consume

indicators.note: to consume is to take in, so the anagram takes in the letter
nuts means crazy, so the letters of munched go wild

explanation.surface: Some Europeans snacked on nuts, eating tons of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like food but is the anagram signal on MUNCHED; 'to consume' puts T inside.
explanation.definitionFit: People from the Netherlands are Europeans.

clue.text: Carrying gun, perhaps, ineffectual person catches headless chicken

indicators.note: catches means holds within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a weed is a feeble, weak person

indicators.note: headless means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a capon is a castrated cockerel raised for eating

explanation.surface: A weakling with a gun manages to catch a running headless chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' removes C from CAPON, leaving APON, which WEED holds.
explanation.definitionFit: To be armed is to carry a weapon, a gun being one example.

clue.text: Shortly cook a pastry dish that's not expensive

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, so the final letter of the cook is dropped

parts.note: a chef is a cook
a pie is a dish with a pastry crust

explanation.surface: A cook will soon make an inexpensive pastry dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shortly' reads as 'soon' but trims CHEF to CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal noun for a low-cost item, something that is not expensive.

clue.text: Mountain break with sea view oddly lacking

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters of sea view are missing, keeping the even ones

parts.note: a rest is a break

explanation.surface: A mountain trip offering a break but with no sea view, oddly enough.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the odd letters of SEA VIEW leaves EVE.
explanation.definitionFit: The highest peak in the world, in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Pause to participate in lung capacity test?

definitions.meaning: to stop and collect yourself before acting
literally, fill the lungs fully as a doctor's test requires

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for stopping to calm down is literally what a patient does when inhaling fully for a test.

clue.text: Support chief facing endless disgrace

parts.note: main means chief or principal

indicators.note: endless means the last letter is removed

parts.note: a taint is a stain or disgrace

explanation.surface: Backing a leader who faces unending disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to support something is to keep it up or uphold it.

clue.text: The entire navy's confused

parts.note: all means the entire amount
read as 'navy is', a fleet's natural place is out on the ocean, away from port

explanation.surface: The whole navy is in a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'navy's' stands for 'navy is', and where a navy is: at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being lost and bewildered is being all at sea.

clue.text: Row of shrubs near hospital boundary

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
an edge is a boundary

explanation.surface: A line of bushes near the boundary of a hospital's grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A planted line of bushes forming a field or garden border.

clue.text: Musicians performing rap hits succeeded

indicators.note: performing suggests the letters of rap hits are acted out in a new arrangement

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for succeeded, used in genealogies

explanation.surface: Musicians who performed rap hits did well.
explanation.definitionFit: Players of a large stringed instrument are musicians.

clue.text: They're against getting involved in important issues

indicators.note: involved in means contained inside the words important issues

explanation.surface: Opponents getting involved in big matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural noun for people who oppose something, campaigners against a cause.

clue.text: Protect small moorland plant river washed away

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: washed away means the river letter is removed

parts.note: heather grows on moorland

explanation.surface: Shielding a little moorland plant from being swept off by a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To cover a blade in a case is to protect it; more widely, to encase or shield.

clue.text: Description of many women idly swimming in Windermere?

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the body of water

parts.note: Windermere is a lake, the largest in England's Lake District

indicators.note: swimming suggests the letters of idly moving about

explanation.surface: Women lazily swimming in Windermere, a lake in England's Lake District.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges IDLY to DYLI, placed 'in' LAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: Refined and genteel, an adjective traditionally applied to well-mannered women.

clue.text: Source of fuel left to burn

parts.note: ignite means to set burning

explanation.surface: Fuel abandoned to be set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Brown coal, a soft coal burned as fuel in power stations.

clue.text: Pants crony put in a drawer

indicators.note: put in means the letter goes inside the jumbled letters
pants is British slang for rubbish, signalling the letters of crony are scrambled

explanation.surface: Underpants that a friend stuffed into a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' is British slang for 'rubbish', the anagram signal; 'drawer' is someone or something that draws.
explanation.definitionFit: A coloured wax stick is a thing that draws, a drawer in the artistic sense.

clue.text: Play here, subsequently stifling expression of disgust

parts.note: present means here, in attendance

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: later means subsequently
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: A play here eventually suppresses a groan of distaste.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1939 comedy for the stage by Noël Coward.

clue.text: Liberal politician, outwardly 'ealthy

indicators.note: outwardly means one piece forms the outside around the other

parts.note: hale means healthy, so with the dropped H of a Cockney accent it loses its first letter
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician who looks healthy, said in a Cockney accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Liberal' looks like the party but is the definition; 'ealthy is healthy with its H dropped, so HALE loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping.

clue.text: Variety of citrus fruit that's dear

definitions.meaning: a hybrid of grapefruit and pomelo, green-skinned and sweet
an affectionate term for a loved one, a darling

explanation.definitionFit: The fruit name is also an endearment like darling or honey.

clue.text: Man, say, needs money to go round Scottish town

indicators.note: to go round means to surround, so the money letters are placed outside

parts.note: pay is money earned
the Isle of Man is an example of an island

explanation.surface: A man needs cash to travel around a town in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, an example of an island.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in Renfrewshire, west of Glasgow, which gave its name to a fabric pattern.

clue.text: Mentioned place to find wine merchant

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a cellar is where wine is stored

explanation.surface: A spoken reference to where a wine merchant can be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader is someone who sells goods, a merchant.

clue.text: Jazz musician's favourite numbers about to make a comeback

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

indicators.note: to make a comeback means to come back, read in the opposite direction

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A jazz musician's favourite tunes are about to return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a comeback' reverses NOS + RE to give ERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Oscar Peterson was a Canadian jazz pianist.
